objective_summary: Computationally nominate a novel synthetic promoter-repressor pair whose promoter retains predicted transcriptional activity and whose repressor is predicted to bind the intended operator more favorably than a defined off-target DNA panel.
target_contexts: Synthetic sigma70-compatible bacterial promoter containing the cognate operator.
off_target_contexts: Shipped natural and synthetic operator panel.
Sequence-scrambled variants of the cognate operator.

success_criteria.statement: The promoter retains computational signals associated with sigma70 transcriptional activity.
The promoter contains a plausible operator site that overlaps the intended regulatory region.
The repressor sequence has plausible composition, complexity, and fold confidence.
The predicted repressor-DNA complex supports the intended cognate interface and base contacts.
success_criteria.measurement_type: protein-DNA structure confidence and contact metrics

success_criteria.statement: The cognate operator scores more favorably than the declared off-target DNA panel.
Final candidates are non-degenerate and retain meaningful sequence diversity.
Final candidates are checked for close similarity to known promoter and protein sequences.

negative_criteria: Reject invalid biological alphabets, excessive homopolymers, and low-complexity sequences.
Reject candidates that fail required promoter, fold, interface, or specificity gates.
Do not claim experimental function, validated binding, or guaranteed orthogonality.
failure_conditions: No candidates survive a required hard gate.
A must-have requirement is neither measured nor explicitly accepted as a limitation.
A blocking critic objection remains unresolved.
The final candidate pool collapses to duplicate or near-duplicate sequences.
required_inputs: Pinned Proto Language and Proto Tools revisions.
Promoter seed FASTA and operator panel.
HTH seed pool and structural template panel.
Approved model access and compute budget before heavyweight execution.
assumptions: The campaign is a benign synthetic regulatory design exercise.
Outputs are computational hypotheses intended for experimental prioritization.
Heavyweight components will not run until their original access requirements are satisfied.
